title: Regular-immersion geometry and intrinsic virtual dimension
statement:
Let schemes and their morphisms be as in [def-pc-scheme], with regularity [def-weil-regular-scheme], finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A regular closed immersion means one whose ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; its codimension is the locally constant length of that sequence, or equivalently the rank of its conormal module. The following hold for Noetherian schemes.

An immersion between regular schemes is regular. Regular closed immersions are preserved by flat base change and composition; their codimensions are preserved by flat base change and add under composition. A section of a separated smooth morphism of relative dimension $r$ is a regular closed immersion of codimension $r$. A scheme smooth over a regular scheme is regular.

A finite-type morphism $f:Y\to X$ between regular affine schemes admits a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_X$; every such immersion is regular. For any factorization $f=pi$ with $i$ a regular closed immersion of codimension $c$ and $p$ smooth of relative dimension $r$ (locally on components), the integer $r-c$ is locally constant and satisfies, for $y\in Y$, $x=f(y)$,
$$r-c=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}-\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y).$$
Dimension and transcendence degree are [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-kun-transcendence-degree], and residue fields are [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus this integer is independent of the factorization. For a quasi-finite $f$ (finite type with finite fibres), the residue extension is finite and its transcendence degree is zero. These assertions include codimension zero, relative dimension zero, and empty schemes; on the empty scheme all pointwise assertions are vacuous.
